description: OpenAPI 2.0 path-operation coverage and exhaustive source-artifact disposition evidence.

scenarios.description: OAS 2.0 defines seven fixed Path Item operation slots and operationId as the unique operation identifier. A simple GET under an absolute schemes/host/basePath target is therefore represented with its literal paths selector (edition analysis N2-03/N2-04).

A required query Parameter and required body Parameter synthesize as one flat protocol-neutral input contract. The body Parameter name remains documentary; the adapter-owned transform constructs the exact parameters/body invocation envelope, while the sole concrete consumes alternative self-selects (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-02, OAPI20-P-03).

Same-named Parameters in different locations preserve both identities by selecting qualified caller keys for the entire non-body parameter set; RFC 6901 escaping remains part of the key convention rather than HTTP routing (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-02).

Two usable concrete consumes declarations preserve two represented alternatives. Because the payload is required, requestMedia is discoverable on the target and on both alternatives without entering the operation input contract (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-03).

A usable https scheme and safe security sibling keep the target representable, while the wss scheme and credential destination colliding with an effective Parameter remain visible as smallest-owner excluded alternatives. Multiple complete security alternatives retain the security selection requirement (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-04).

Successful exact and default response schemas are projected as alternative whole-body output contracts. Response Header declarations do not create output members, and synthesis invents no status/header context binding (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-03).

Request projection removes an optional readOnly property, while response projection preserves that property. Draft-04 boolean exclusiveMinimum is translated to the equivalent numeric JSON Schema 2020-12 assertion without weakening it (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-01).

A range response key is upstream-invalid on the 2.0 line and removes only its owning operation, accounted invalid. Tolerant synthesis retains an unrelated valid sibling and accounts both positions exhaustively rather than refusing the whole source (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-03).

A discriminator annotation has no equivalent Core JSON Schema assertion under the synthesis policy. The operation remains callable, while a lossy projection entry makes the omission durable instead of silently claiming full representation (OAPI20-S-01).

A response Header Object array cannot use collectionFormat multi. The upstream-invalid header declaration is accounted invalid at its own projection position, while the operation remains represented because response headers create no output member under this binding (OAPI20-S-01, OAPI20-P-03).

A request-body Schema Object whose `allOf` branches intersect emptily is a WELL-FORMED upstream declaration that admits no instance, and the JSON-lane position it governs is accounted `represented` with `fullyRepresented: true`. The governing dialect's validity condition for `allOf` is structural only — a non-empty array whose elements are valid schemas — and neither that dialect nor any accepted OAS edition gives satisfiability any role, so nothing about `allOf: [{type: string}, {type: object}]` is upstream-invalid; Core OBI-D-17 says the same from the other side, requiring no proof of satisfiability for a schema to be well-formed. §12.2 admits `invalid` only where the declaration is upstream-invalid, and §3.2 keeps `invalid` and `excluded` apart on exactly that line, so this position is neither: the emitted OBI carries the declaration as written, nothing is projected away, and coverage stays fully represented. The `application/json` lane is selected by media type rather than by the resolved declaration, which is why no admission test gates this position; the intersecting sibling is the control that keeps the scenario about the empty intersection rather than about `allOf`. Where the resolved declaration DOES select carriage — the character-data and raw-octet lanes, a multipart part, a urlencoded property — §9.1's stated no-admissible-candidate rule excludes the alternative instead, which is a different rule with a different status and is not asserted here.

Path correspondence preserves the upstream-validity boundary on the 2.0 line. A template expression with no effective path parameter is a binding exclusion because OAS 2.0 does not forbid it, while an effective path parameter with no expression is upstream-invalid. The unrelated valid operation remains represented, and fullyRepresented is false only because the excluded upstream-valid target counts against it.
A source whose sole addressable operation is upstream-invalid is still accepted and synthesized; the target is accounted invalid rather than being reclassified as a whole-source refusal.

A failure-only Response defect and an impossible 204 body schema are subordinate coverage loss: both operations remain represented while the exact Response projections are accounted invalid and excluded.
Header-name synthesis confines a non-token optional name to one excluded projection, propagates a non-token required name to its target, and excludes a processor-owned Transfer-Encoding target.
A default-only Responses Object is valid; the operation and its fallback Response projection remain fully represented.
A non-token OAS 2.0 response Header Object key is subordinate excluded coverage; without a required-header field on this edition, its response alternative and operation remain represented.
A WebSocket-only artifact leaves the operation represented and records the server configuration requirement needed to obtain a dispatchable HTTP target.
A required fixed-destination collision excludes only its credential alternative and preserves a safe OR sibling; the same collision with an optional parameter is not a static exclusion.
An unrepresentable multipart property name is accounted at its media-alternative owner while the target and an unrelated operation remain represented.
A required request Content-Encoding parameter on a target with no surviving request lane excludes only that target; an unrelated operation remains represented.

Synthesis removes an optional non-token header projection before caller-key uniqueness is computed, so the surviving same-named query parameter remains represented under its unqualified operation-input key.

Out-of-enum authored schemes are invalid only at their alternatives: a valid HTTPS sibling remains usable, while an operation with no valid artifact scheme remains represented with its complete-URL recovery requirement.
A response media range carrying a case-insensitive q parameter is excluded only at that alternative, while a valid sibling and the target remain represented.
An effective caller-owned Accept Header Parameter suppresses generated Accept, so a q-bearing produces range and its target remain represented.
